prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity visual concept for the first viewport of Luke's Chinese interactive portfolio website, edge-to-edge wide desktop 16:10, no browser frame, no device mockup. The entire screen is an oblique orthographic view of a dense lotus pond made from precise visible ordered-dithering pixels and stippled ink tones, inspired by retro GPU Bayer dithering, with sculptural depth, not a watercolor painting. The water is the empty warm yellow xuan-paper ground with extremely fine film-like grain and delicate fibers. Large, medium and small lotus leaves overlap naturally in several layers and cover about three quarters of the viewport, with uneven openings of paper-water. Leaves are charcoal to pale ink-grey, never green. A few softly sculpted muted dusty pink and grey-purple lotus flowers among the leaves. Vermilion, orange-gold and ivory-spotted koi swim underneath, mostly occluded by the leaves: show glimpses of several natural tapered koi with delicate fins, clear eyes and sinuous tails. Preserve a believable top-oblique view, subtle material shading represented with 4–6 stippled tone levels, crisp pixel lattice, no smooth gradients, no outlines around everything. The scene is the working website: one visible koi is hover-enlarged slightly in an open patch and has a tiny legible label 'MOSIC' below it; another partially visible fish may be labeled 'Meet Countdown'. No headline, no biography, no cards, no badges, no grid of feature text. At the bottom corner only a small understated Chinese hint '拨开荷叶，随鱼入内'. Sophisticated composition, dense upper and side foliage, asymmetrical breathing gaps; quiet, crafted, tactile. No photorealistic pond water, no green leaves, no neon, no cartoon emoji, no interface panel boxes, no giant text. This is a visual reference for a live procedural Three.js scene.
